cases.situation: My college roommate Sophie's mom died. We haven't talked in a couple of years, but I knew her mom, she used to send us care packages with lemon bars during finals.
cases.reply: Sophie, I'm so sorry about your mom. I still think about those lemon bars showing up every finals week, she fed half our floor. Thinking of you and your dad. No need to reply to this.
cases.note: A years-long gap doesn't need explaining; the specific memory is what she'll keep.

cases.situation: 我手下的员工小李，父亲昨天去世了，他已经请假回老家。我想以领导的身份给他发个微信。
cases.reply: 小李，听说你父亲去世了，非常难过。工作的事一点都不用操心，你手上的项目我已经安排小周接着跟。需要休多久就休多久。想着你和家人，不用回复。
cases.note: 作为领导，最具体的帮助就是把工作接过去，并且明说不用回复。

cases.situation: My best friend Marco's wife Elena died a year ago this Saturday. I want to text him something that day.
cases.reply: Thinking about you and Elena today. I still smile about her making us redo the barbecue because we'd 'insulted the ribs'. I'm around all weekend if you want company. No need to reply.
cases.note: The anniversary message matters more than the first one, because most people have stopped sending them.

cases.situation: 好朋友阿杰的爸爸三周前去世了。我这几周隔几天就发消息问他怎么样，昨天他回我：我没事，别老问了。我有点慌，不知道还要不要再联系他。
cases.reply: 好，我不追着问了。我在，不会走开。周六下午我把你爱吃的老街卤味挂你家门把手上，不用开门，也不用回我。
cases.note: 被推开时不辩解也不消失：接受他的话，把“问候”换成不需要回应的陪伴。之后隔一两周发一句，不带问题。

cases.situation: 同事阿May养了13年的狗豆豆昨天走了，她今天请了假。我们关系不错，我见过豆豆几次，它每次都叼着拖鞋来迎人。想在微信上跟她说一声。
cases.reply: 阿May，听说豆豆走了，真的很难过。我一直记得它叼着拖鞋跑来迎人的样子，13年，它在你身边过得特别幸福。工作这边你别惦记，周三的周会我帮你汇报。不用回我，就是想着你。
cases.note: 宠物离世也是真的失去：叫它的名字，说一个具体的记忆，给一个实际的帮助，并明说不用回复。

cases.situation: Soy gestora autónoma. Mi clienta de hace ocho años, Pilar, me escribió que su marido Andrés murió el sábado y que se va a retrasar con los papeles del trimestre, que vencen el 20 de octubre.
cases.reply: Pilar, lo siento muchísimo por Andrés. Me acuerdo de lo orgulloso que estaba cuando abrió el segundo taller en 2022. Del trimestre no te preocupes: presento yo la declaración del 20 de octubre con lo que ya tengo, y lo que falte lo vemos en noviembre. No hace falta que me contestes.
cases.note: Con una clienta, la oferta concreta es quitarle el trabajo de encima, no ofrecer ayuda en general.

cases.situation: My sister-in-law Amy texted me that she lost the baby at 11 weeks. She and my brother had only told close family. I have no idea what to say.
cases.reply: Amy, I'm so sorry. Thank you for telling me. There's nothing you need to say or do, and you don't have to be okay. I'll leave a pot of soup on your step Thursday evening; no need to answer the door or reply to this.
cases.note: Don't explain the loss ('at least it was early', 'it wasn't meant to be'); presence plus one practical thing is the whole message.

cases.situation: Our elderly neighbour Margaret's husband Frank died last week. We're not close with her, but Frank waved at our kids from the porch every morning and once fixed my son's bike without being asked. I want to leave a card in her mailbox.
cases.reply:
Dear Margaret,
We were so sorry to hear about Frank. Our boys still call him 'the waving man'; every morning on the way to school he was on the porch, and he once spent a whole Saturday fixing Theo's bike chain without being asked. Our street won't be the same. Tom will bring your bins in on Thursday evenings for as long as it helps. No need to reply to this card.
With love,
Anna, Tom, Theo and Max
cases.note: A neighbour you barely know still gets the name, one specific memory and one practical thing that needs no answer from her.

cases.situation: I just found out on LinkedIn that my former manager Denise's husband Paul died in July. It's been over two months and I feel awful I didn't say anything. I met Paul at our team Christmas parties.
cases.reply: Denise, I only just heard about Paul, and I'm so sorry. I still remember him at our team Christmas parties, the only person who could get the whole finance team onto the dance floor. Thinking of you. No need to reply to this.
cases.note: Late is fine, and often lands better, because the messages have dried up by month two. One clause for the timing, no paragraph of guilt.

cases.situation: I'm going to the funeral of my coworker Dev's father on Friday. I never met his dad, but Dev talked about him a lot, especially how they went to every cricket test at Edgbaston together. What do I actually say to Dev in the line after the service?
cases.reply: Dev, I'm so sorry about your dad. I keep thinking about the two of you at Edgbaston every summer. You don't need to say anything, I just wanted to be here.
cases.note: In a receiving line, two or three sentences. If you never met the person, something the griever told you about them does the work of a memory.

cases.situation: 一起共事了十年的同事老周上周突发心梗走了。我没见过他太太，想请同事转一封信给她，说说老周在单位是什么样的人。
cases.reply: 周太太您好，我是老周在设计院的同事李明，和他共事了十年。听到消息，我们都很难过。老周是我们组最靠得住的人，谁的图纸出了问题，他都会留下来陪着改到半夜，第二天还拎一兜包子来。他常说起您和女儿，说周末最盼的就是一家人去爬紫金山。我们都会记得他。单位这边的手续，您告诉王主任一声，我们来跑。您不用回信。
cases.note: 写给不认识的家属，最珍贵的是具体的往事和他在别人眼里的样子；先说明自己是谁，免去回复。

cases.situation: 大学好友小薇刚告诉我她确诊了乳腺癌，下周一开始化疗。她一个人在杭州工作，我在上海。不知道该说什么，怕说错话。
cases.reply: 小薇，谢谢你愿意告诉我，听到这个消息我真的很难过。你一直是我们几个里最能扛事的人，但这次你不用一个人扛。化疗第一周的周六我去杭州陪你，买菜做饭跑腿都交给我。这条不用回，周末我再给你发消息。
cases.note: 不要说“一定会好的”，也不要讲别人的抗癌故事；给一个具体的陪伴安排，并免除她回复的负担。

cases.situation: My friend Kara's younger brother Josh died by suicide last week. I met Josh a few times; at her birthday last year he spent ages teaching me to make proper espresso. I don't know what to say or whether to mention how he died.
cases.reply: Kara, I'm so sorry about Josh. I keep thinking of him at your birthday, patiently teaching me to pull an espresso shot and laughing at my first three attempts. I'm dropping dinner at yours on Thursday evening, no need to answer the door. You don't have to reply to this, I'm just here.
cases.note: Say his name and a real memory, don't ask what happened or offer explanations, and if she brings up how he died, follow her lead.

cases.situation: My teammate Rosa comes back to the office on Monday after three weeks off; her mum died of cancer. We sit next to each other and she used to tell me about her mum's allotment. What do I say when she walks in?
cases.reply: Rosa, welcome back. I'm so sorry about your mum. I keep thinking of her and those allotment courgettes you used to bring in. I've put the Hendry notes from the last three weeks in one doc, so you don't have to dig through your inbox. No need to talk about any of it unless you want to.
cases.note: First day back: say it once, briefly, then let her decide whether it comes up again; catching her up on work is the concrete help.
